subscription_products.product_name: Big Red High Protein Dog Food, 50-lb bag
subscription_products.subscription_rationale: Daily food is the primary consumable. For a very active 11-month-old, 50 lb pitbull I estimate ~4 cups/day to fuel energy and maintain condition. Typical kibble density ≈ 4 cups per pound → 50 lb bag ≈ 200 cups. Consumption math: 4 cups/day × 30 days = 120 cups/month. 200 cups ÷ 120 cups/month = 1.67 months per bag → plan autoship every ~7 weeks. This avoids running out while keeping orders cost-effective.
subscription_products.personalized_note: Thor is 11 months and very active — this 50-lb high-protein bag will keep his energy up for yard workouts and training without having you reorder every week. We can shorten or lengthen the frequency as his appetite stabilizes.

Estimate 12–15 treats/day while actively training: 15/day × 30 = 450 treats/month. A 6-oz training pouch of small 'mini' treats typically contains roughly 300–400 mini treats → 1 bag ≈ 0.7–0.9 months. Autoship every 3–4 weeks keeps fresh rewards on hand during this high-training stage.
subscription_products.personalized_note: Thor is in that prime adolescent training window — these small, soft treats are perfect for rapid-fire reinforcement during recall and impulse-control practice in the yard.

subscription_products.product_name: BARK Nutty Lil' Starz Peanut Butter & Jelly Flavored Soft & Chewy Dog Training Treats, 6-oz bag

subscription_products.personalized_note: Thor will appreciate alternating flavors during training — rotating these on autoship keeps him excited when you ask for that next great recall.

overall_strategy: Because Thor is an 11‑month-old, high-energy 50 lb pitbull with strong chew strength and a large yard, we prioritize a mixed strategy: set up autoship for the true consumables you’ll use repeatedly (main food sized for his intake, several training-treat options, waste bags, dental pastes and paw care items) with frequencies based on estimated monthly depletion; buy durable, seasonal and safety items once now (water fountain, cooling mat, chew‑proof leash, no‑pull harness, durable toys, grooming & calming gear) to solve immediate setup and weather-driven needs. Journey stage (Month 2, new rescue adolescent) calls for both setup essentials and higher treat volume for training — so autoship keeps training rewards and hygiene supplies on-hand while one-time purchases secure long-lasting safety, enrichment and comfort for Thor. Revisit quantities in 4–8 weeks once you have real consumption data and adjust autoship cadences (especially food and treats) to match Thor's actual intake.
